record.original_question: Among all trees of order n, is the adjacency spectral gap minimized by some double comet C(k, ell)?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 19 (Jovović-Koledin-Stanić [87]). Among all trees of order n, the spectral gap is minimized for some double comet.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $T$ be a simple undirected tree on $n$ vertices, and let $A(T)$ denote its adjacency matrix. Order the eigenvalues of $A(T)$ as $\lambda_1(T) \geq \lambda_2(T) \geq \cdots \geq \lambda_n(T)$. The (adjacency) spectral gap of $T$ is defined as $\lambda_1(T) - \lambda_2(T)$.

For integers $k \geq 1$ and $\ell \geq 1$ with $k + \ell + (n - k - \ell) = n$, the double comet $C(k, \ell)$ is the tree obtained from a path $P_{n-k-\ell}$ on $n-k-\ell$ vertices by attaching $k$ pendant edges to one endpoint of the path and $\ell$ pendant edges to the other endpoint.

Question: For every integer $n \geq 4$, is the minimum of the spectral gap $\lambda_1(T) - \lambda_2(T)$ over all trees $T$ on $n$ vertices attained by some double comet $C(k, \ell)$?
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture, due to Jovović, Koledin, and Stanić (Ars Mathematica Contemporanea, 2018), is supported by computer verification for trees with at most 20 vertices, and partial theoretical results about double comets are known, but no general proof appears in the literature. The problem is still considered open.

status_evidence.title: Trees with small spectral gap
status_evidence.snippet: Authors conjecture, on the basis of computer search, that the spectral gap of trees on n vertices is minimized by some double comet; verified for n ≤ 20.
status_evidence.claim: Conjecture stated and verified computationally for small n; no general proof given.

status_evidence.title: Graphs with small spectral gap (ELA)
status_evidence.snippet: Earlier related work on graphs with small spectral gap by Stanić.
status_evidence.claim: Background line of work; full conjecture for trees remains unresolved.
